preconditions: Choose status, pick, report saving, delegation or receiver maintenance; a status request is not necessarily read-only.
Resolve discovery scope and review the llm_backends declaration when registry refresh can occur.
Use the existing task authorization and trusted endpoint configuration for delegation; non-loopback delegation requires HTTPS and a token.
Receiver maintenance additionally depends on operator-configured named commands and their own consequences.

expected_effects.effect: status/machines may refresh backend discovery; status --subnet forces a refresh.
expected_effects.scope: Discovery targets and the llm_backends registry in the toolkit checkout.
expected_effects.basis: machines refreshes when fresh or no registry entries exist; status passes fresh=scan_subnet.
expected_effects.impact: Produces network requests and replaces the shared registry through llm_backends; cached status can also discover when no entries remain.
expected_effects.verification: Use mocked discovery with a temporary registry; verify subnet propagation and the cache-miss path.

expected_effects.effect: pick(lru) and status with chat candidates update last-used state before a task is delegated.
expected_effects.scope: The current user's .botte-cluster.json and later LRU selections.
expected_effects.basis: status calls pick(lru); pick writes a timestamp through _save_state. pick(latency) does not write that state.
expected_effects.impact: Monitoring itself can change which backend receives future work. Best-effort writes and concurrent callers do not provide a reservation or lease.
expected_effects.verification: Use two fixture backends and temporary LRU state; call status twice and inspect the changed recommendations without delegating.

expected_effects.effect: status --save writes a report containing machine and model details.
expected_effects.scope: The caller working directory's .botte/reports and report consumers.
expected_effects.basis: cli status invokes report.save only when requested.
expected_effects.impact: Retains infrastructure metadata and consumes storage; the saved recommendation can become stale.
expected_effects.verification: Save a mocked status report in a temporary working directory and inspect the destination and retained fields.

expected_effects.effect: delegate posts task text to a configured receiver and returns a truncated HTTP response.
expected_effects.scope: Selected agent endpoint, transmitted task/token, receiver logs and any work accepted there.
expected_effects.basis: delegate validates the endpoint and token before POST; delegated=True means a response was received, not that its payload reports task success.
expected_effects.impact: The receiver may reject, accept or execute work. An interrupted request can leave unknown remote state; no request identity or deduplication protocol is supplied.
expected_effects.verification: Mock HTTP replies containing both successful and failed task results; distinguish transport receipt from independently observed completion.

expected_effects.effect: Serving the reference receiver listens for tasks; permitted maintenance runs operator-defined subprocesses.
expected_effects.scope: Receiver host, listening socket, inherited process environment and resources touched by configured commands.
expected_effects.basis: agent exposes named read actions and _run_named requires a configured command plus confirm=True.
expected_effects.impact: Consumes service resources and can mutate the host through approved commands. Output may disclose host data; process exit alone is not task proof.
expected_effects.verification: Inject a runner for a named fixture command; verify unknown/unconfirmed commands do not launch and inspect result/error output.

downstream_effects.effect: Registry and LRU writes affect later routing even when status launched no task.
downstream_effects.scope: Later callers sharing the backend registry or user LRU state.
downstream_effects.basis: Status refreshes metadata and records its LRU recommendation as last used.
downstream_effects.impact: Repeated monitoring can perturb load distribution; last-used time is not observed workload or completion evidence.
downstream_effects.verification: Replay two status observations and compare later selections; do not infer active load from LRU alone.

downstream_effects.effect: Receiver work may continue or leave partial mutations after caller timeout.
downstream_effects.scope: Remote task resources and any dependent operations.
downstream_effects.basis: The delegation client supplies neither transactional rollback nor remote cancellation/acknowledgment reconciliation.
downstream_effects.impact: Blind retries can duplicate maintenance, work and costs.
downstream_effects.verification: Use receiver-side task evidence and actual resource state to choose a bounded retry or stop.

reversibility.strategy: Reconcile discovery/LRU state separately from remote task resources. Restore only appropriate retained state; rollback of maintenance belongs to the selected command and receiver.
residual_effects: Remote work, output disclosures and consumed resources are not undone by a caller timeout.
LRU state has no history or atomic cross-process reservation.

retry.check_before_retry: Identify whether retry means another status selection, a saved report or a remote POST. For uncertain delegation, inspect the receiver result and affected resources first.
retry.stop_condition: Stop duplicate remote requests while completion is uncertain or endpoint/token configuration remains unresolved; resolve scope using the existing task authority.

required_scope: Existing authorization for the discovery range, shared state files, output destination and remote task. A named whitelist, confirm flag or declared contract does not create task authority.

analysis.summary: Status has observable scheduling side effects; delegation is a transport handoff whose business outcome must be verified separately.
uncertainties: llm_backends and report implementations are external to these local source hashes.
Custom receiver implementations and maintenance command configurations determine additional effects.
No exactly-once delegation, remote cancellation or fleet rollback is provided.

reuse.target: Build a target-scoped cluster observation and reconciliation report.
reuse.rationale: Backend grouping and explicit transport results supply useful inputs when separated from verified remote outcomes.
adaptations: Account for status-induced LRU writes and registry changes.
Use target receiver evidence for completion; do not reuse delegated=True as a success label.
reuse.validation: Replay empty/two-backend status fixtures plus rejected and timed-out receiver replies before target deployment.
